question.text: When <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>200</mn><mo> </mo><mi>mL</mi></math> of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>0</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>2</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">M</mi></math> acetic acid is shaken with <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>0</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>6</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">g</mi></math> of wood charcoal, the final concentration of acetic acid after adsorption is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>0</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>1</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">M</mi></math>. The mass of acetic acid adsorbed per gram of carbon is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">g</mi></math>.

solution.text:
Mole of acetic acid absorbed (on 0.6 gram charcoal) =(0.2 X200)10-3 – (0.1 X 200)10-3=20 X 10-3

Weight of CH3COOH absorbed (on 0.6 gram charcoal)=(20 X10-3 ) 60 = 1200 X10-3  gram = 1.2 gram

Mass of CH3COOH absorbed per gram=1.20.6=2grams
